contracts.forbidden_condition: Invoking execute_tool for a BLOCKed get_account_details or query_compliance_rules call, causing the executor's outbound HTTP request (_http_get to {GATEWAY_URL}/stream/recent or _http_post to {A5_RAG_URL}) to be issued despite the BDH block.

contracts.protected_operation: Dispatch and execution of LLM-proposed get_account_details and query_compliance_rules tool calls from the llm_escalation_node agent loop.
contracts.protected_resource: The TOOL_EXECUTORS-dispatched executors _execute_get_account_details (GET {GATEWAY_URL}/stream/recent?n=200) and _execute_query_compliance_rules (POST {A5_RAG_URL} compliance query).
contracts.protection_obligation: BDH BLOCK verdicts must likewise prevent execution of LLM-proposed non-critical tool calls (get_account_details, query_compliance_rules) in the escalation node, so that no outbound HTTP effect — the gateway /stream/recent GET or the A5 compliance-RAG POST — is issued for a blocked call.
scope_limits: Same client-side, fail-open, single-call-site limits as the critical-tool gating contract: enforcement exists only in the audited llm_escalation_node loop and defaults to ALLOW when BDH is unreachable (orcestrator/nodes.py:68-70).

These are read-only outbound lookups; blocking them prevents information retrieval, not persistent mutation — the consequential state-changing stratum for this guard is covered by the database-stratum contract.

Which BDH rules apply differs by tool: Rules 1 (context), 2 (registry/schema), and 4 (loop) apply to both; Rule 3 (drift) applies to get_account_details (account_id present in args) but not to query_compliance_rules; Rule 5 (idempotency) applies to neither (not in CRITICAL_TOOLS, bdh_service/main.py:83).

contracts.commit_point: The execute_tool(tool_name, tool_args) call in the ALLOW branch of llm_escalation_node (orcestrator/nodes.py:357-361), followed by the persistent Redis commits inside the executors (mcp_tools.py:260-276 XADD+HSET for block_account; mcp_tools.py:298-310 XADD for escalate_to_investigator).
contracts.declared_mechanism: _bdh_audit pre-flight POST to the BDH watchdog /audit endpoint invoked for every proposed tool call before dispatch (orcestrator/nodes.py:44-67, 346), with an explicit audit_res.get('status') == 'BLOCK' branch (nodes.py:348-356) that skips execute_tool and instead appends a 'BDH_WATCHDOG_BLOCKED: <reason>' tool message to the conversation.
contracts.forbidden_condition: Invoking execute_tool — and thereby the executor's persistent Redis writes — for a tool call whose _bdh_audit result has status BLOCK; i.e., any BLOCKed block_account or escalate_to_investigator call reaching the dispatch at nodes.py:361 and committing its pathway:events XADD or blocked:{account_id} HSET.

Whether a swallowed Redis write failure (persisted=False) should still count as a committed critical action for BDH idempotency is undetermined.
Whether pathway:events writes should ultimately be classified as database persistence or message delivery to downstream consumers is a classification judgment the supplied source does not settle.
contracts.protected_operation: Dispatch and execution of LLM-proposed critical MCP tool calls from the llm_escalation_node agent loop: block_account (pathway:events 'account_blocked' XADD plus blocked:{account_id} HSET) and escalate_to_investigator (pathway:events 'investigator_escalation' XADD).
contracts.protected_resource: The TOOL_EXECUTORS-dispatched executors _execute_block_account and _execute_escalate_to_investigator and the persistent Redis records they write: pathway:events stream entries (account_blocked / investigator_escalation) and the blocked:{account_id} hash.
contracts.protection_obligation: In the LLM escalation node (Node 4), a BDH BLOCK verdict on an LLM-proposed critical tool call (block_account or escalate_to_investigator) must prevent the call from reaching execute_tool, so that no account-block or investigator-escalation effect is committed to persistent Redis storage; a blocked call may only be surfaced back to the LLM as a 'BDH_WATCHDOG_BLOCKED' tool message.
scope_limits: Client-side enforcement: applies only to the audited loop in llm_escalation_node; any other code path invoking execute_tool or TOOL_EXECUTORS directly is outside the cited guard.
Fails open: when the BDH service is unreachable, _bdh_audit returns ALLOW (orcestrator/nodes.py:68-70), so the BLOCK-prevents-execution guarantee holds only while BDH responds within the 3s timeout.

The gate precedes dispatch only; there is no independent interlock between BDH idempotency state and actual persistence success — executors swallow Redis write failures and return persisted=False (mcp_tools.py:278-279, 312-313), while BDH already marked the critical action executed at audit-ALLOW time (bdh_service/main.py:201-202).

Classification: pathway:events XADD is modeled here as a persistent database mutation (Redis stream with maxlen); the same records also function as a message stream consumed downstream (BDH consumer, A8 SAR drafter, A10 feedback loop per mcp_tools.py:255-256, 292-293).

contracts.commit_point: Construction and return of the AuditResponse verdict by audit_endpoint — the finish() status computed by audit_llm_tool_call after rule evaluation — which the gateway consults before executing the tool.
contracts.declared_mechanism: Deterministic five-rule audit in audit_llm_tool_call (context-exhaustion, tool-registry/schema validation, state-drift, infinite-loop, critical-tool idempotency) over per-anomaly Redis SessionState (_get_session/_save_session), registered as the FastAPI handler for POST /audit returning AuditResponse(status, reason); each BLOCK also emits a bdh_alert event to pathway:events via _emit_bdh_alert.
contracts.forbidden_condition: audit_llm_tool_call or the /audit endpoint returning ALLOW (or any non-BLOCK verdict) when the audited LLM tool call: exceeds the 5-step context (main.py:152-155); names a tool not in ALLOWED_TOOLS or raises ValidationError against its schema (main.py:158-169); carries an account_id that drifts from session.target_account_id (main.py:172-178); repeats the exact same tool+args call a 3rd time (main.py:190-193); or names a critical tool already present in session.executed_critical_actions (main.py:196-200).
pending_binding_information: Whether callers other than orcestrator/nodes.py llm_escalation_node POST /audit (the bdh_service docstring says 'the gateway's LangGraph Node 4') cannot be fully confirmed from the supplied views.
Whether the 300s session TTL can expire mid-anomaly (long-running escalations) and reset step/idempotency counters is undetermined.

Concurrency semantics of simultaneous audits for the same anomaly_id (read-modify-write race on bdh:session:{anomaly_id} with no locking in source) are unspecified and could weaken the five-rule guarantees.
contracts.protected_operation: Pre-flight audit decision (ALLOW/BLOCK with reason) for every LLM-proposed tool call, performed before the gateway's LangGraph Node 4 executes the tool.
contracts.protected_resource: The five-rule verdict path of audit_llm_tool_call exposed at POST /audit, backed by per-anomaly session state persisted at bdh:session:{anomaly_id}; the verdict gates execution of the four registered MCP tools (get_account_details, query_compliance_rules, block_account, escalate_to_investigator).
contracts.protection_obligation: The BDH watchdog's POST /audit pre-flight check must return BLOCK with a reason (never ALLOW) for any LLM-proposed tool call that violates any of the five deterministic audit rules — (1) context exhaustion: session tool_call_count exceeding 5 per anomaly; (2) hallucinated tool: tool_name absent from ALLOWED_TOOLS or args failing the tool's Pydantic schema; (3) state drift: tool_args.account_id differing from the session's target_account_id; (4) infinite loop: the identical call reaching repeat_count 3; (5) idempotency: a CRITICAL_TOOLS member (block_account, escalate_to_investigator) already recorded as executed for the anomaly — and must return ALLOW only when all five checks pass.
scope_limits: Verdict-only obligation: this contract covers the ALLOW/BLOCK decision returned by the BDH service; enforcement that the caller actually skips execution is a separate orchestrator-side contract.
State-drift (Rule 3) fires only when 'account_id' is present in tool_args (bdh_service/main.py:172), so escalate_to_investigator calls keyed on transaction_id are not drift-checked.

Rule 5 marks a critical tool as executed at audit-ALLOW time (bdh_service/main.py:201-202), not at the actual tool-effect commit, so the idempotency ledger tracks audited-allowed proposals rather than committed effects.
Session state expires after 300 seconds (bdh_service/main.py:125), bounding the context-exhaustion and idempotency windows per anomaly.
The /audit endpoint is unauthenticated with permissive CORS (bdh_service/main.py:315-320); agent mediation rests on the orchestrator dataflow, not on any authenticated caller binding.
Fail-open behavior lives caller-side (orcestrator/nodes.py:68-70); this contract does not govern callers that ignore or never obtain the verdict.
